---
title: "Measuring overlaps"
subtitle: "`src/overlap.ts`: how deep cells press into each other and into the walls"
---

Real bacteria do not pass through each other. In a physics engine, bodies pressed together always
overlap a little, since the solver only pushes them apart after they touch. How deep they overlap
is the best single measure of whether the solver is doing its job, so the program measures it:
for every pair of touching cells, and for cells against the walls. The solver settings were tuned
against this measure, and long runs are validated with it (see the
[overlap report](reports/overlap-report.md)).

The measurement runs on the live simulation, at full precision. The recorded files are rounded to
two decimals (orientation to 0.01·π), which alone can move a cell's tip by about 0.03, more than the
overlaps being measured.

## The target

The deepest overlap between two cells should stay below 8% of the cell width. The target was 5%
at first; it was relaxed to 8% in exchange for fewer solver iterations, i.e. faster steps. It
applies after a warm-up of 3000 steps, since the random initial placement overlaps heavily and
needs time to relax.

```{.typescript #overlap-target}
export const OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION = 0.08;
export const OVERLAP_WARMUP_STEPS = 3000;
```

## The measurements

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `step`, `cells` | when the measurement was taken, and how many cells there were |
| `overlappingPairs` | pairs of cells that overlap at all |
| `maxDepth` | the deepest cell–cell overlap |
| `meanDepth` | the mean over the overlapping pairs (0 if there are none) |
| `p99Depth` | the 99th percentile over the overlapping pairs |
| `pairsOverTarget` | pairs deeper than the target |
| `maxWallDepth` | the deepest overlap of a cell with a wall or wall triangle |
| `maxAt`, `maxWallAt` | where the deepest overlaps are: the midpoint between the two cells' centres, and the centre of the cell in the wall |

```{.typescript #overlap-stats}
export interface OverlapStats {
  step: number;
  cells: number;
  overlappingPairs: number;
  maxDepth: number;
  meanDepth: number;
  p99Depth: number;
  pairsOverTarget: number;
  maxWallDepth: number;
  maxAt: { x: number, y: number };
  maxWallAt: { x: number, y: number };
}
```

The [runner](cli.qmd) can log one row per snapshot as CSV, for the analysis scripts in `tools/`:

```{.typescript #overlap-csv}
export const OVERLAP_CSV_HEADER =
  "step,cells,overlapping_pairs,max_depth,mean_depth,p99_depth,pairs_over_target,max_wall_depth,max_depth_fraction_of_width,max_x,max_y,wall_x,wall_y";

export function overlapCsvRow(s: OverlapStats, width: number): string {
  return [s.step, s.cells, s.overlappingPairs, s.maxDepth.toFixed(5), s.meanDepth.toFixed(5), s.p99Depth.toFixed(5),
    s.pairsOverTarget, s.maxWallDepth.toFixed(5), (s.maxDepth / width).toFixed(5),
    s.maxAt.x.toFixed(2), s.maxAt.y.toFixed(2), s.maxWallAt.x.toFixed(2), s.maxWallAt.y.toFixed(2)].join(",");
}
```

## Capsules and segments

A capsule is the set of points within distance $r$ of a line segment, its *axis*: here, the segment
between the centres of the two end caps. Two capsules therefore overlap exactly when their axes are
closer than $2r$, and the depth of the overlap is

$$
d = 2r - \operatorname{dist}(\text{axis}_1, \text{axis}_2) .
$$

Likewise a cell overlaps a wall (a segment of zero thickness) by $r - \operatorname{dist}$. So the
whole measurement comes down to the distance between two segments.

### Distance between two segments

The function below is the classic algorithm from Christer Ericson's *Real-Time Collision Detection*
(section 5.1.9). The points on the two segments are $P_1 + s\,d_1$ and $P_2 + t\,d_2$ with
$s, t \in [0, 1]$. Minimising the squared distance over $s$ and $t$ gives a small linear system;
its solution is clamped to the segments, and when one parameter is clamped, the other is recomputed
for the clamped value. Segments of (nearly) zero length are points and are handled first. The
function returns the *squared* distance, so that the common case, two cells far enough apart, needs
no square root.

```{.typescript #overlap-segment-distance}
export function segmentDistanceSquared(
  p1x: number, p1y: number, q1x: number, q1y: number,
  p2x: number, p2y: number, q2x: number, q2y: number,
): number {
  const d1x = q1x - p1x, d1y = q1y - p1y;
  const d2x = q2x - p2x, d2y = q2y - p2y;
  const rx = p1x - p2x, ry = p1y - p2y;
  const a = d1x * d1x + d1y * d1y;
  const e = d2x * d2x + d2y * d2y;
  const f = d2x * rx + d2y * ry;
  const EPS = 1e-12;
  let s: number, t: number;
  if (a <= EPS && e <= EPS) {
    s = 0; t = 0;
  } else if (a <= EPS) {
    s = 0; t = clamp01(f / e);
  } else {
    const c = d1x * rx + d1y * ry;
    if (e <= EPS) {
      t = 0; s = clamp01(-c / a);
    } else {
      const b = d1x * d2x + d1y * d2y;
      const denom = a * e - b * b;
      s = denom > EPS ? clamp01((b * f - c * e) / denom) : 0;
      t = (b * s + f) / e;
      if (t < 0) { t = 0; s = clamp01(-c / a); } else if (t > 1) { t = 1; s = clamp01((b - c) / a); }
    }
  }
  const dx = p1x + d1x * s - (p2x + d2x * t);
  const dy = p1y + d1y * s - (p2y + d2y * t);
  return dx * dx + dy * dy;
}
```

```{.typescript #overlap-clamp}
function clamp01(v: number): number {
  return v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v;
}
```

## The meter

Testing every pair of ~1750 cells would take 1.5 million segment distances per measurement.
Instead, the meter sorts the cells into a grid and only tests cells in neighbouring grid squares.
It runs at every snapshot (in the runner when an overlap log is requested, and always in the
browser) and, in the browser's diagnostic view, on every frame in which the simulation has moved,
so it keeps its arrays between calls and grows them only when the colony grows.

```{.typescript #overlap-meter}
export class OverlapMeter {
  <<overlap-meter-buffers>>

  <<overlap-measure>>

  <<overlap-ensure>>
}
```

The buffers hold, per cell, the two ends of its axis ($a$ and $b$) and its centre ($c$); the grid
square of each cell, and the cells ordered by grid square; the start of each square in that order;
and the depths of the overlapping pairs, for the percentile.

```{.typescript #overlap-meter-buffers}
private ax = new Float64Array(0); private ay = new Float64Array(0);
private bx = new Float64Array(0); private by = new Float64Array(0);
private cx = new Float64Array(0); private cy = new Float64Array(0);
private binOf = new Int32Array(0); private order = new Int32Array(0);
private binStart = new Int32Array(0);
private depths = new Float64Array(0);
```

```{.typescript #overlap-ensure}
private ensure(n: number): void {
  if (this.ax.length >= n) { return; }
  const m = Math.max(n, 2 * this.ax.length, 1024);
  this.ax = new Float64Array(m); this.ay = new Float64Array(m);
  this.bx = new Float64Array(m); this.by = new Float64Array(m);
  this.cx = new Float64Array(m); this.cy = new Float64Array(m);
  this.binOf = new Int32Array(m); this.order = new Int32Array(m);
}
```

`measure` takes the simulation, the cell radius and the depth that counts as "over target". An
optional callback receives every overlapping pair, as indices into the order of `forEachCell`; the
browser uses it to highlight the pairs. The measurement has four stages:

```{.typescript #overlap-measure}
public measure(sim: Simulation, radius: number, targetDepth: number,
  onPair?: (i: number, j: number, depth: number) => void): OverlapStats {
  <<overlap-gather>>

  <<overlap-bin>>

  <<overlap-pairs>>

  <<overlap-walls>>

  <<overlap-result>>
}
```

### 1. Gather the axes

A cell's long axis is its local $y$ axis, which points along $(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta)$. The ends
of the axis are the centre plus and minus half the length along it. The longest cell is noted too:
it sets the size of the grid squares.

```{.typescript #overlap-gather}
const n = sim.cellCount;
this.ensure(n);
const { ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy } = this;
let k = 0, maxLength = 0;
sim.forEachCell((x, y, angle, length) => {
  const h = length / 2, ux = -Math.sin(angle) * h, uy = Math.cos(angle) * h;
  ax[k] = x - ux; ay[k] = y - uy; bx[k] = x + ux; by[k] = y + uy; cx[k] = x; cy[k] = y;
  if (length > maxLength) { maxLength = length; }
  k++;
});
```

### 2. Sort the cells into a grid

Two cells can only overlap if their centres are closer than $\ell_\text{max} + 2r$: half a length
each, plus a radius each. With grid squares that wide, overlapping cells always sit in the same or
in adjacent squares. The cells are sorted by square with a counting sort: count the cells per
square, turn the counts into start positions (a running sum), then place each cell at its square's
next free position.

```{.typescript #overlap-bin}
const size = maxLength + 2 * radius + 1e-6;
let minX = Infinity, minY = Infinity, maxX = -Infinity, maxY = -Infinity;
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  if (cx[i] < minX) { minX = cx[i]; } if (cx[i] > maxX) { maxX = cx[i]; }
  if (cy[i] < minY) { minY = cy[i]; } if (cy[i] > maxY) { maxY = cy[i]; }
}
const nx = n > 0 ? Math.floor((maxX - minX) / size) + 1 : 1;
const ny = n > 0 ? Math.floor((maxY - minY) / size) + 1 : 1;
const bins = nx * ny;
if (this.binStart.length < bins + 1) { this.binStart = new Int32Array(bins + 1); }
const binStart = this.binStart, binOf = this.binOf, order = this.order;
binStart.fill(0, 0, bins + 1);
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  const b = Math.floor((cy[i] - minY) / size) * nx + Math.floor((cx[i] - minX) / size);
  binOf[i] = b;
  binStart[b + 1]++;
}
for (let b = 0; b < bins; b++) { binStart[b + 1] += binStart[b]; }
const fill = binStart.slice(0, bins);
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { order[fill[binOf[i]]++] = i; }
```

### 3. Test the pairs

Each cell is tested against the cells in its own and the eight surrounding squares, and each pair
only once (the other cell's index must be larger). A quick check on the distance between the
centres skips most pairs before the segment distance is computed. For every overlapping pair, the
depth is recorded and the statistics updated.

```{.typescript #overlap-pairs}
const touch = 2 * radius, touch2 = touch * touch;
let pairs = 0, sum = 0, maxDepth = 0, overTarget = 0;
const maxAt = { x: NaN, y: NaN }, maxWallAt = { x: NaN, y: NaN };
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  const bxi = binOf[i] % nx, byi = (binOf[i] - bxi) / nx;
  for (let gy = Math.max(0, byi - 1); gy <= Math.min(ny - 1, byi + 1); gy++) {
    for (let gx = Math.max(0, bxi - 1); gx <= Math.min(nx - 1, bxi + 1); gx++) {
      const b = gy * nx + gx;
      for (let o = binStart[b]; o < binStart[b + 1]; o++) {
        const j = order[o];
        if (j <= i) { continue; }
        const ddx = cx[i] - cx[j], ddy = cy[i] - cy[j];
        if (ddx * ddx + ddy * ddy > size * size) { continue; }
        const d2 = segmentDistanceSquared(ax[i], ay[i], bx[i], by[i], ax[j], ay[j], bx[j], by[j]);
        if (d2 >= touch2) { continue; }
        const depth = touch - Math.sqrt(d2);
        if (this.depths.length <= pairs) { const grown = new Float64Array(2 * pairs + 64); grown.set(this.depths); this.depths = grown; }
        this.depths[pairs++] = depth;
        sum += depth;
        if (depth > maxDepth) { maxDepth = depth; maxAt.x = (cx[i] + cx[j]) / 2; maxAt.y = (cy[i] + cy[j]) / 2; }
        if (depth > targetDepth) { overTarget++; }
        if (onPair) { onPair(i, j, depth); }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 4. Test the walls

The walls are the chamber's edges and the sides of the wall triangles, as segments. Only cells
close enough to reach a wall are tested: within half the longest length plus a radius of a side
wall or the top wall, with a margin of 1.5 because the triangles stick one unit into the chamber.
The depth is measured from the wall line, so a cell whose axis crosses a wall counts as depth
$r$.

```{.typescript #overlap-walls}
let maxWallDepth = 0;
const reach = maxLength / 2 + radius + 1.5;
const segments = wallSegments();
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  if (cx[i] > -50 + reach && cx[i] < 50 - reach && cy[i] < 200 - reach) { continue; }
  for (let w = 0; w < segments.length; w += 4) {
    const d2 = segmentDistanceSquared(ax[i], ay[i], bx[i], by[i], segments[w], segments[w + 1], segments[w + 2], segments[w + 3]);
    if (d2 < radius * radius) {
      const depth = radius - Math.sqrt(d2);
      if (depth > maxWallDepth) { maxWallDepth = depth; maxWallAt.x = cx[i]; maxWallAt.y = cy[i]; }
    }
  }
}
```

### The result

```{.typescript #overlap-result}
return {
  step: sim.stepCount, cells: n, overlappingPairs: pairs, maxDepth,
  meanDepth: pairs > 0 ? sum / pairs : 0,
  p99Depth: percentile(this.depths.subarray(0, pairs), 0.99),
  pairsOverTarget: overTarget, maxWallDepth, maxAt, maxWallAt,
};
```

## Helpers

The wall segments never change, so they are built once from the [chamber data](model.qmd#the-chamber-geometry)
and cached, as a flat list of coordinates $x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2, \ldots$

```{.typescript #overlap-wall-segments}
let wallSegmentCache: Float64Array | null = null;

function wallSegments(): Float64Array {
  if (wallSegmentCache) { return wallSegmentCache; }
  const list: number[] = [];
  for (const [a, b] of CHAMBER.edges) { list.push(a.x, a.y, b.x, b.y); }
  for (const t of CHAMBER.triangles) {
    for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) {
      const a = t.vertices[k], b = t.vertices[(k + 1) % 3];
      list.push(a.x + t.offset.x, a.y + t.offset.y, b.x + t.offset.x, b.y + t.offset.y);
    }
  }
  wallSegmentCache = Float64Array.from(list);
  return wallSegmentCache;
}
```

The percentile sorts a copy of the depths (typed arrays sort numerically):

```{.typescript #overlap-percentile}
function percentile(values: Float64Array, q: number): number {
  if (values.length === 0) { return 0; }
  const sorted = Float64Array.from(values).sort();
  return sorted[Math.min(sorted.length - 1, Math.floor(q * sorted.length))];
}
```
